<ConflictType> — No conflict — All documents affirm that flowers existed during the Mesozoic era when dinosaurs lived, with varied supporting details.

All retrieved documents consistently support that flowering plants existed in the dinosaur era. d1 explicitly states flowers have been on Earth for about 140 million years since the Early Cretaceous, a period dinosaurs inhabited [d1]. d3 reports a flower fossil dated to 260 million years old, before the Mesozoic began, placing flowers earlier than dinosaurs [d3]. d4 and d5 indicate orchids (a flower family) arose around 80 million years ago and co-existed with dinosaurs [d4,d5]. d6 mentions flowers with fragrant scents from the Cretaceous period [d6]. d7 and d8 also mention flowers as part of Mesozoic flora [d7,d8]. Only d2, discussing butterflies, notes that colorful butterflies evolved after dinosaurs, but its main point about butterflies coexisting with dinosaurs does not contradict the floral evidence [d2]. All sources converge on the affirmative answer.

The documents collectively provide clear affirmative evidence: flowers existed before and during the age of dinosaurs. The oldest flower fossil is 260 million years old (Pre-Mesozoic) [d3], and flowering plants diversified in the Cretaceous (145–66 million years ago) when dinosaurs thrived [d1,d4,d5,d6,d8]. Even d7 notes flowers as part of Mesozoic life. Thus, the answer is unequivocally yes.

Yes, flowers existed in the age of dinosaurs. Flowering plants (angiosperms) were present during the Mesozoic era when dinosaurs lived [d7]. The oldest known flower fossils date back to 260 million years ago, predating the dinosaur era [d3]. During the Cretaceous period (145–66 million years ago), which dinosaurs inhabited, flowers diversified and were present, with orchids estimated to have arisen around 80 million years ago [d4,d5]. Evidence also shows dinosaurs could have encountered fragrant flowers in the Cretaceous [d6]. Therefore, flowers coexisted with dinosaurs.
